segs: in the Tekiasa of Rav in Bavel,
That is, "U'vechein" has the numerical value of seventy-two,
which alludes to the seventy-two Names
that emerge from the three verses
and the holy Zohar said earlier
that they are "the crown of the Avos."
And this is what it said: "corresponding to these three."
(פְּרִי עֵץ חַיִּים, שַׁעַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה פֶּרֶק ז)
(Pri Etz Chaim, Shaar Rosh Hashanah, chapter 7)
הוּא נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
who sanctified the Name of Heaven in the fiery furnace.
corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom,
whose attribute is "the Fear of Yitzchak."
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
שֶׁאָמַר בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.
who said, "Baruch shem kevod malchuso l'olam va'ed."
that they correspond to Avraham and Yitzchak — is understandable;
אַךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר עַל 'וּבְכֵן תֵּן כָּבוֹד'
but what he said about "U'vechein tein kavod,"
we need to understand the connection.
The matter is based on what they said in the Pesikta
(Pesikta Rabbasi 39, for Rosh Hashanah, the section beginning "Yelamdeinu"):
"'Shout for joy to the God of Yaakov' (Tehillim 81:2):
'לֹא הִבִּיט אָוֶן בְּיַעֲקֹב וְגוֹ׳' (בַּמִּדְבָּר כג, כא).
'He has not beheld iniquity in Yaakov,' etc. (Bamidbar 23:21).
What did Bilam see to mention Yaakov,
and not Avraham and not Yitzchak, etc.?
He saw that dross came forth from Avraham, etc.,
לְפִיכָךְ לֹא הִזְכִּיר לְאֶחָד מִן הָאָבוֹת
Therefore he did not mention any one of the Avos
'Shout for joy to the God of Yaakov,' Selah."
with respect to what is said:
"He has not beheld iniquity in Yaakov," etc. —
in that his bed was complete.
But what kind of reason is this
for what is said, "Shout for joy to the God of Yaakov"?
However, it is stated in the Pesikta
(פְּסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי מ, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל):
(Pesikta Rabbasi 40, the section beginning "Speak to the Children of Yisrael"):
that you should blow the shofar on Rosh Hashanah,
so that when you tremble at the blowing of the shofar,
you will prepare yourselves for teshuvah."
in order to make the heart tremble,
"Shall a shofar be blown in a city and the people not tremble?"
And through the awe and the fear
'אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת ה׳' (תְּהִלִּים קיב, א) —
"'Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem' (Tehillim 112:1) —
אַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה כְּשֶׁהוּא אִישׁ וְכוּלֵּי.
fortunate is one who does teshuvah while he is still a man in his prime, etc."
That is, when a person takes to heart
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
immediately awe and fear will come upon him
(as the Hagahah writes at the beginning of Orach Chaim, 1:1);
and then, out of the awe,
he is ashamed of the past and does teshuvah.
And this is the business of the blowing of the shofar:
to arouse all the hearts of Yisrael to teshuvah.
And this works through his bed being complete,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְשׁוּרִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that is, that Yisrael are bound at the root to Hashem Yisbarach,
"It is revealed and known before You
that our will is to do Your will, etc."
And this is what they said (Vayikra Rabbah 29:4):
"'Fortunate is the people who know the teruah' (Tehillim 89:16) —
וְכִי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין יוֹדְעִין לְהָרִיעַ?
do the nations of the world not know how to sound a teruah?
How many horns they have, etc.!
אֶלָּא שֶׁיּוֹדְעִין לְפַתּוֹת אֶת בּוֹרְאָם בִּתְרוּעָה.
Rather, it means that they know how to win over their Creator with the teruah."
were commanded regarding the mitzvah of shofar,
and if the nations of the world too
had been commanded regarding the mitzvah of blowing the shofar,
for they have many horns and trumpets;
so why are there none among them who "know the teruah"?
רַק הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת שֶׁעַל יְדֵי קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר
Rather, the arousal that comes through the sound of the shofar
who are bound at the root to Hashem Yisbarach —
"that our will is to do Your will."
And this is what Yaakov accomplished
Which is not so with the nations of the world:
even if they were commanded regarding the shofar
לֹא הָיָה מוֹעִיל לָהֶם הַקּוֹל שׁוֹפָר כְּלָל.
the sound of the shofar would not help them at all.
And this is what is said:
"He has not beheld iniquity in Yaakov,
he spoke of Yaakov and Yisrael,
And it is written right after it:
"And the teruah of the King is in him";
and it is stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 55, 88b)
that the teruah is from the side of both of them,
which is the attribute of Yaakov.
וְכֵן כָּתַב בְּפֵירוּשׁ בַּתִּקּוּנִים אַחַר כָּךְ:
And so it writes explicitly in the Tikkunim afterward:
"'And the teruah of the King is in him' —
here you have it: the teruah is in Yaakov."
And this is what it said in the Pesikta:
"Therefore he did not mention any one of the Avos
except Yaakov: 'Shout for joy to the God of Yaakov'" —
for the main benefit of the blowing of the shofar
who are the seed of Yaakov,
whose bed was complete, as stated.
And this is the intent of the Arizal,
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
שֶׁאָמַר בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד;
who said "Baruch shem kevod malchuso l'olam va'ed";
when his sons said to him:
"Just as in your heart there is only One,
so in our heart there is only One";
בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה פָּתַח יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ וְאָמַר
at that moment Yaakov Avinu opened and said,
That is, the glory of the Kingship of Heaven
is revealed only when there is a complete nation,
שֶׁמַּכִּירִין וּמְקַבְּלִין עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
who recognize and accept the yoke of His Kingship, blessed be His Name.
And this is why we ask of Hashem Yisbarach:
"U'vechein, Hashem, grant honor to Your people, etc.,
and good hope to those who seek You" —
in the vein of what is said
(in the Musaf of Rosh Hashanah, the blessing of Zichronos):
"For those who seek You will never stumble,
וְלֹא יִכָּלְמוּ לָנֶצַח כָּל הַחוֹסִים בָּךְ'.
nor will any who take refuge in You ever be put to shame."
"My God, I am ashamed and humiliated
to lift my face to You,
כִּי עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ רָבוּ עַד לְמַעְלָה רֹּאשׁ וְגוֹ׳' —
for our iniquities have risen above our heads," etc. —
at lifting one's face before Hashem Yisbarach.
"For those who seek You will never stumble" —
that is, that they will be saved from the yetzer hara forever,
in the vein of what they said (Sukkah 52a):
and automatically, "nor will they ever be put to shame —
all who take refuge in You."
"and good hope to those who seek You."
However, a person's inclination overpowers him,
וְאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזֵר לוֹ
and were it not for the Holy One, blessed be He, who helps him,
and one needs prayer for this.
וְלִפְעָמִים גַּם כֹּחַ הַתְּפִלָּה אֵין לוֹ,
And sometimes he does not even have the strength for prayer,
to be able to pray before Him;
"and an opening of the mouth to those who hope to You,"
in the vein of what is said (Tehillim 51:17):
that Hashem Yisbarach should open our lips in prayer,
so that we can pray before Him.
And through this we will merit the redemption,
that there will be "joy to Your land, etc.,
and the flourishing of pride for Dovid Your servant."
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם עַ״ב עֲתִידִין לְהִגָּאֵל,
through the Name of seventy-two they are destined to be redeemed,
"As in the days of your going out from the land of Egypt
And the time for this through teshuvah
"'Today — if you will listen to His voice'" (Tehillim 95:7).
But the main time is on Rosh Hashanah,
שֶׁאָז מִתְעוֹרְרִין עַל יְדֵי הַשּׁוֹפָר לִתְשׁוּבָה.
when people are aroused to teshuvah by the shofar.
And as we said from the Pesikta
that on Rosh Hashanah they are redeemed from the Angel of Death.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
And this is the meaning of what the holy Zohar cited above said:
that the three "U'vechein," which have the numerical value of seventy-two,
הַמְּרוּמָּז בִּפְסוּקֵי וַיִּסַּע וַיָּבֹא וַיֵּט, כָּאָמוּר.
as alluded to in the verses Vayisa, Vayavo, Vayet, as stated.
it is stated in Pri Etz Chaim (ibid.)
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
that it corresponds to Dovid HaMelech, alav hashalom.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר בַּתִּקּוּנִים (תִּקּוּן כב סז, א):
This is based on what it says in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, 67a):
"And this is the secret of Shabbos:
the Shin — which is Vayisa, Vayavo, Vayet —
which are included in the Bas, etc.";
is a chariot for the attribute of Malchus, the aspect of "Bas."
And it appears that just as on Shabbos,
"Shin–Bas: the Bas is crowned with the Avos,"
likewise "the Bas is crowned with the Avos."
And we ask: "U'vechein, the righteous will see and rejoice,"
אַךְ עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי יג, ט):
but on this it is said (Mishlei 13:9):
one merits to straighten the heart,
and then "for the upright of heart, joy" (Tehillim 97:11).
And this is why we say: "and the upright will exult,
and the pious will rejoice in song" —
song is the revelation of joy.
And then "iniquity will close its mouth,
and all wickedness will vanish like smoke" —
for then the yetzer hara will be swallowed up,
together with the Satan and the Angel of Death,
and as they said in the Pesikta
שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִגְאָלִים מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, כָּאָמוּר;
that on Rosh Hashanah they are redeemed from the Angel of Death, as stated.
וְאָז 'וְתִמְלוֹךְ אַתָּה הוּא ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְבַדֶּךָ':
And then: "And You, Hashem our God, will reign alone."
אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב מד, א וְעוֹד):
It is stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 44a, and elsewhere):
"'And it was the day,' etc. (II Melachim 4:11) —
was the festival day of Rosh Hashanah."
And for this reason it is stated in the Or Zarua
that "hayom" without qualification alludes to Shabbos;
and as stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36, 77b):
"'And there was light' — this is Rosh Hashanah";
and in the Midrash Rabbah (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4),
עַל פָּסוּק (תְּהִלִּים כז, א) 'ה׳ אוֹרִי וְיִשְׁעִי':
on the verse (Tehillim 27:1) "Hashem is my light and my salvation":
so seemingly, how can they coexist —
which are two opposites in one subject?
However, in truth both are right together,
for precisely through the distress and the distance
שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ כָּל אֶחָד בְּנַפְשׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם זֶה,
that each person feels in his soul on this day,
that it is the time of the revelation of His Kingship, may He be blessed,
as we say: "U'vechein, instill Your fear
upon all that You have created,
and all the works will fear You," etc.;
וְכָל אֶחָד כְּפִי שֶׁמַּכִּיר אֶת נִגְעֵי לְבָבוֹ,
and each one, according to how he recognizes the afflictions of his heart —
from truly accepting the yoke of the Kingship of Heaven —
from this comes the greatness of the distress and fear
which is called in the holy Zohar in several places
"the Second Day, the Fear of Yitzchak."
And in proportion to the distress and the awe,
from this there flows into the soul an illumination from Above,
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים קוֹדֶם תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר הַפָּסוּק
And this is why, before the blowing of the shofar, we say the verse
"From the straits I called out to Hashem" (Tehillim 118:5):
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַקְּרִיאָה בַּלֵּב מִן הַמֵּצַר,
for through the calling out in the heart from the straits,
which is the illumination from Above
that flows from the blowing of the shofar.
And as stated in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 16b):
"A year that is poor at its beginning
that Yisrael make themselves poor and their heart is humbled before the Omnipresent.
For through feeling the distance within himself,
meaning that he has a future,
for immediately he feels the illumination
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ הַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
And this is the meaning of the Midrash Rabbah cited above:
שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא הַתְחָלַת הַבְהָקַת הָאוֹר
on Rosh Hashanah is the beginning of the shining of the light
toward the sprouting of the salvation,
and the culmination of the salvation, in revealed form,
And as stated in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 30:7)
"For with You is forgiveness, that You may be feared":
"From Rosh Hashanah the forgiveness waits for You —
in order to place Your awe upon Your creatures."
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת עֶצֶם הַיְשׁוּעָה לְעֵילָּא
That is, in truth the essence of the salvation Above
not yet revealed in the soul,
until Yom Kippur — "that You may be feared."
שֶׁנִּמְצָא עוֹד הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בַּנֶּפֶשׁ,
for the awe of Rosh Hashanah is still present in the soul,
and draw near out of the distance.
וּמִזֶּה בָּאִים לְהִתְגַּלּוּת הַיְשׁוּעָה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
And from this they come to the revelation of the salvation on Yom Kippur,
so that there becomes revealed to every soul
closeness to Hashem Yisbarach in completeness.
"We learned: 'And the judgment of His people Yisrael,
דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ' (מְלָכִים א ח, נט).
each day's matter on its day' (I Melachim 8:59).
'Day on its day' — what is it?
אֶלָּא הָנֵי תְּרֵי יוֹמִין דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
Rather, these are the two days of Rosh Hashanah.
Because they are two courts of judgment
the upper judgment, which is harsh,
with the lower judgment, which is soft."
וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת ה׳ עִלָּאָה וְה׳ תַּתָּאָה,
That is, the aspect of the upper Hei and the lower Hei,
and both of them dwell in the heart.
For the lower fear as well,
on the verse "when he has no heart" (Mishlei 17:16) —
but has no fear of Heaven.
And Binah, which is "Binah is the heart,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּפֶתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ, הַקְדָּמַת תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר),
as written (in Pesach Eliyahu, Introduction to Tikkunei Zohar),
is when the fear has already entered
the inwardness of the point within the heart.
And these are the aspects of the Written Torah
עַל יוֹם ב׳ שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
regarding the second day of Rosh Hashanah
in the verse "each day's matter on its day,"
which was said by Shlomo HaMelech, alav hashalom,
שֶׁהוּא הָיָה בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
who was the aspect of the Oral Torah —
the lower Wisdom, the wisdom of Shlomo.
And also the allusion in the Torah:
yet in truth, by Torah law there is no difference;
רַק לִרְמֹז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִדְּרַבָּנָן.
it is only to allude to the Oral Torah, rabbinic law.
has a great root in the Torah.
Therefore, even in the time of the Beis HaMikdash
for the reason that witnesses came
מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ל, ב),
and they are like one long day.
For in truth the two aspects
as it says, "each day's matter on its day":
"'The word of Hashem' (Amos 8:12) — this is halachah";
'הָלוֹךְ וְדַבֵּר' (מְלָכִים ב ב, יא) בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
"'Walking and talking' (II Melachim 2:11) — in words of Torah."
דְּיוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן הוּא נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
The first day corresponds to the aspect of the Written Torah,
and then an illumination flows from Above
even into the inwardness of the point in the heart,
from the aspect of the Hidden World,
as stated (in the holy Zohar there)
the Fear of Yitzchak, the concealed judgment, etc.,
and both of them are as one."
And on the second day one comes,
עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּלּוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
through the revelation of the Oral Torah,
likewise to the aspect of the point in the heart,
"For with much wisdom comes much anger" —
שֶׁכְּדֵי לְהַכְנִיעַ הָרוֹב כַּעַס שֶׁל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
meaning that to subdue the "much anger" of the yetzer hara,
it is done through the "much wisdom,"
which is the aspect of the Oral Torah.
the illumination of the inwardness of the point in the heart,
as stated (in the holy Zohar there)
"'Fortunate is the people who know the teruah;
Hashem, in the light of Your countenance they walk':
the secret of the teruah, as it says,
'You will smash them with an iron rod' (Tehillim 2:9);
and all those who know the secret of the teruah
will merit and draw near to walk
in the light of the countenance of the Holy One, blessed be He;
and this is the primordial light
that the Holy One, blessed be He, stored away for the righteous."
הִנֵּה אָמְרוּ חֲזַ״ל (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יח, א)
עַל פָּסוּק (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, ו) 'דִּרְשׁוּ ה׳ בְּהִמָּצְאוֹ וְגוֹ׳':
on the verse (Yeshayah 55:6) "Seek Hashem while He may be found," etc.:
between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur."
(וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כא, ד; שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים כז)
עַל פָּסוּק (תְּהִלִּים כז, א) 'ה׳ אוֹרִי וְיִשְׁעִי':
on the verse (Tehillim 27:1) "Hashem is my light and my salvation":
an illumination comes to the heart
from the revelation of the Kingship of Heaven.
And this is why it says "my light" specifically,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר שָׁם בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל):
as it says there in the Midrash (the Shocher Tov cited above):
אָדָם מַדְלִיק אֶת הַנֵּר בְּפַלְטִין שֶׁלּוֹ וְכוּלֵּי,
"A man lights a lamp in his palace, etc.,
אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵן,
but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so;
let My children see, and let My enemies not see.
And He already did such a thing in Egypt:
'They did not see one another,' etc.,
וּלְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר' (שְׁמוֹת י, כג);
'but for all the Children of Yisrael there was light' (Shemos 10:23);
'and there was the cloud and the darkness';
'For behold, darkness will cover the earth,'
but for Yisrael, 'and upon you Hashem will shine.'"
שֶׁהוּא זְמַן הִתְגַּלּוּת כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
which is the time of the revelation of the glory of His Kingship, may He be blessed,
נוֹפֵל מִזֶּה הַפַּחַד עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
fear falls from this upon the nations of the world,
as it is said: "U'vechein, instill Your fear," etc.,
וְכָל הָרִשְׁעָה כּוּלָּהּ כֶּעָשָׁן תִּכְלֶה וְגוֹ׳,
"and all wickedness will vanish like smoke," etc.;
"U'vechein, the righteous will see and rejoice";
and all of Yisrael are called righteous,
For to Yisrael an illumination comes into the heart
from the revelation of the Kingship of Heaven,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה קָרוֹב לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
through which one becomes close to Hashem Yisbarach
and begins to "seek Hashem while He may be found."
And this is "whom shall I fear?" —
for he has nothing to fear;
but the lamp of the wicked flickers out."
And this is "Hashem is the stronghold of my life — whom shall I dread?"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (נְחֶמְיָה ח, י):
as was said on Rosh Hashanah (Nechemiah 8:10):
"For the joy of Hashem is your strength";
for the aspect of strength and might
brings to gladness and joy in the heart.
And it says further in the Midrash cited above:
'Send Your light and Your truth; they will guide me.'"
of the illumination of the Kingship of Heaven on Rosh Hashanah,
the point of truth shines forth in the souls of Yisrael;
and this is "Your light and Your truth."
כִּי בְּהֶאָרָה זוֹ שֶׁל נְקוּדַת הָאֱמֶת
for with this illumination of the point of truth
Hashem Yisbarach guides the souls of Yisrael
during the Ten Days of Teshuvah,
that He be near to those who call upon Him,
עַד גְּמַר הִתְגַּלּוּת הַיְשׁוּעָה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
until the completion of the revelation of the salvation on Yom Kippur.
"Fortunate is the people who know the teruah;
Hashem, in the light of Your countenance they walk" —
for through the illumination of the countenance
of the teruah of Rosh Hashanah,
which lights up the point of truth in the heart,
one merits to walk from level to level
when the salvation is revealed tangibly.
And this is "Send Your light and Your truth; they will guide me."
עוֹד שָׁם בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב) הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
Further, there in the Midrash (Shocher Tov) cited above:
'Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.'
אִם נֶאֱמַר נֵר, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר אוֹר?
If it says 'lamp,' why does it say 'light'?
וְאִם נֶאֱמַר אוֹר, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר נֵר?
And if it says 'light,' why does it say 'lamp'?
כְּשֶׁאֲנִי מַתְחִיל בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, מְעַט וְכוּלֵּי,
When I begin in words of Torah, it is a little, etc.;
many gates open up for me, etc."
from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur:
on Rosh Hashanah the illumination of the Torah begins
from the source, like a lamp,
and afterwards, from the second day onward,
when the revelation of the salvation comes, as mentioned above.
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז גַּם כֵּן הַפָּסוּק אַחַר כָּךְ:
And to this the following verse also alludes:
"Hashem is the stronghold of my life — whom shall I dread?"
to the bestowal of words of Torah,
"Hashem will give strength to His people."
And so it is said in Nechemiah (8:10):
"For the joy of Hashem is your strength" —
referring to the bestowal of words of Torah;
for this took place on Rosh Hashanah,
"on the first day of the seventh month."
"And they read in the book, the Torah of God, clearly,
giving the sense, and they understood the reading" (ibid. 8:8);
that is, the bestowal of the aspect of the Written Torah,
which is from the aspect of "Chochmah is the brain"
and this is "the Torah of God, clearly."
"And on the second day" the people "gathered
to gain insight" in the Torah —
זֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל הַשְׁפָּעַת בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
this alludes to the bestowal of the aspect of the Oral Torah,
which comes through the understanding of the heart,
and this is "to gain insight in the Torah."
And this is the root of the holiness
יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
of the second Yom Tov day of Rosh Hashanah —
the aspect of the bestowal of the Oral Torah.
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּתּוֹסָפוֹת (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יט, ב, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל מִימוֹת)
And as stated in Tosafos (Rosh Hashanah 19b, s.v. "Mimos")
that "from the days of Ezra onward
we have not found Elul extended,"
that it was extended in that year
when Ezra came up from Bavel,
since it says here "and on the second day."
And as is known, Ezra was the beginning
of the Men of the Great Assembly,
שֶׁהָיוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
who were the root of the revelation of the Oral Torah.
Therefore there was then the imprint
of the aspect of the Oral Torah
עַל יְדֵי יוֹם ב׳ דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
through the second day of Rosh Hashanah.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּכָל יְמֵי הַבַּיִת שֵׁנִי
And afterwards, throughout the days of the Second Temple,
only the first day was sanctified,
based on the sighting of the new moon,
מִתַּקָּנַת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וָאֵילָךְ
from the enactment of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai onward
they decreed and instituted observing two days.
כִּי מֵאָז נִתְיַיסְּדָה בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עַל מְכוֹנָהּ
For from then on the aspect of the Oral Torah was set on its foundation
through the disciples of Shammai and Hillel,
שֶׁהָיָה מַחְלְקוֹתָם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם (אָבוֹת ה, יז),
whose dispute was for the sake of Heaven (Avos 5:17),
וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים (עֵירוּבִין יג, ב).
and "these and these are the words of the living God" (Eruvin 13b).
And this is the essence of the Oral Torah,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה נוֹבֵעַ וְנִתְרַבֶּה עַד דּוֹרֵי דוֹרוֹת.
from which it flows and increases for all generations.
קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁנֵי יָמִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
the holiness of the two days of Rosh Hashanah
for all generations forever, for this allusion.
